review_evidence: Item-by-item review for observation versus imagination, clue-based inference, age fit, unseen independent and assessment contexts, deterministic masterclass answers, and flexible creative grading.
title: A Show of Clouds
source_note: Aligned to the NCERT chapter title and themes of observing clouds, noticing changing shapes, and using imagination to describe nature. All Zidd observations, comparisons, prompts, and feedback are original.

levels.title: Observe what clouds do
levels.focus: find visible details about cloud colour, shape, and movement
levels.teaching_goal: Read short sky observations and separate what is seen from what is imagined.

guided_check.teaching_block: An observation tells what eyes can notice: colour, shape, size, or movement. An idea such as it may rain is a guess. Answer with the detail the watcher actually sees.
guided_check.passage: Mira sees one white cloud stretch into a long thin line. It drifts above the trees.
guided_check.prompt: Which detail tells the cloud's shape?

bridge.teaching_block: Read all the details, then match the question word. How it moves is different from where it is.
bridge.passage: Grey clouds slide slowly from the hill toward the lake.

masterclass.teaching_block: A scene can change over time. Use the time clue to choose the later observation.
masterclass.passage: At first, two small clouds were apart. Soon they joined to make one wide cloud.
accepted_answers: the clouds join into one wide cloud

independent_check.teaching_block: Answer without choices. Use only what the observer reports, not a weather guess.
independent_check.passage: A dark cloud covers the sun for a minute, then moves east and lets the light return.
independent_check.prompt: Which direction does the cloud move?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer careful observation to soap bubbles. Name the visible change, not its cause.
transfer_check.passage: A large bubble rises, becomes smaller, and pops above the sink.
transfer_check.prompt: What happens just before the bubble pops?

levels.title: Use clues to imagine a cloud shape
levels.focus: infer an imagined object from shape and action clues
levels.teaching_goal: Connect several cloud clues to a sensible imagined shape and explain the clue used.

guided_check.teaching_block: When we imagine a picture in a cloud, we match more than one clue. A long neck and four legs fit some animals better than a boat. Check every clue.
guided_check.passage: The cloud has four soft legs and a very long neck reaching upward.
guided_check.prompt: What might the cloud look like?

bridge.teaching_block: Look for the strongest shape clue. Wings stretching sideways can suggest a bird even if the cloud is not a real bird.
bridge.passage: Two wide parts spread from a small middle shape as the cloud glides across the sky.

masterclass.teaching_block: Use both shape and movement. A pointed front and a long body moving across the sky fit one choice best.
masterclass.passage: A narrow cloud has a pointed nose and a long body. It seems to race toward the horizon.
masterclass.prompt: What does the cloud most resemble?

independent_check.teaching_block: Make an inference from a fresh cloud description. Name a sensible object and mention the clue that supports it.
independent_check.passage: One end of the cloud curls like a handle, while the other part is round and deep.
independent_check.prompt: What might the cloud look like, and why?

concept_slots.description: Identifies a cup, mug, or similar handled container.
Uses the curled handle and round deep part as evidence.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use shape clues in a shadow-puppet scene, not the sky. Name the imagined animal and one supporting detail.
transfer_check.passage: On the wall, two pointed shadows rise like ears above a round head.
transfer_check.prompt: What animal might the shadow look like, and what clue helps you?

concept_slots.description: Identifies a cat, rabbit, or fox as a reasonable pointed-ear animal.
Mentions the two pointed ear shapes.

levels.title: Understand words for a changing sky
levels.focus: infer and use drift, gather, vanish, pale, and enormous
levels.teaching_goal: Use context to understand words that describe cloud movement, colour, size, and change.

guided_check.teaching_block: Nearby actions can explain a sky word. If a cloud drifts, it moves gently rather than rushing. Test the meaning in the whole sentence.
guided_check.passage: The tiny cloud drifts slowly with the breeze, moving gently above the field.

bridge.teaching_block: A result can reveal the new word. If nothing remains, vanished must mean disappeared.
bridge.passage: The sun came out after the last grey cloud vanished from the sky.

masterclass.teaching_block: Use a comparison clue for size. Enormous means much bigger than large, not merely bright.
masterclass.passage: An enormous cloud spread across nearly the whole sky and made the houses look tiny.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the colour contrast to infer the word.
independent_check.passage: The morning cloud was pale, almost white, unlike the dark cloud behind it.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the word meaning in a crowd scene. The context is new, but the idea of coming together is the same.
transfer_check.passage: Families gather near the stage until many people are standing together.

levels.title: Build a vivid cloud sentence
levels.focus: choose describing words and arrange them into a clear comparison
levels.teaching_goal: Use adjectives and like comparisons to create accurate, well-ordered sky sentences.

guided_check.teaching_block: A describing word tells colour, size, shape, or feeling. Find the word that adds a picture to the naming word cloud.
guided_check.passage: A fluffy cloud floats over the playground.

bridge.teaching_block: A like comparison joins a real observation to an imagined picture. Keep like between the cloud and the image.
bridge.passage: The round cloud looks ___ a silver coin.

masterclass.teaching_block: Check word order and meaning. The sentence should name the cloud, give an action, then add the comparison.
masterclass.passage: Words: cloud / the / like / sails / a ship
options: The cloud sails like a ship.
Like the cloud a ship sails.
A sails ship the cloud like.
accepted_answers: The cloud sails like a ship.
the cloud sails like a ship

independent_check.teaching_block: Arrange the words without choices. Keep both describing words before clouds.
independent_check.passage: Words: slow / grey / clouds / drift / west

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same sentence-building skill for leaves. Keep the comparison at the end.
transfer_check.passage: Words: the / spins / leaf / like / a wheel
accepted_answers: the leaf spins like a wheel
the leaf spins like a wheel.

levels.title: Describe an imagined sky scene
levels.focus: write an observation and an imaginative comparison without confusing them
levels.teaching_goal: Write concise sky descriptions that include a seen detail and a supported imagined shape.

guided_check.teaching_block: A strong sky sentence begins with what is seen, then adds what it looks like. It does not claim the cloud is truly an animal or object.
guided_check.passage: Seen: a broad white cloud with two bumps. Imagined: a camel.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence keeps observation and imagination clear?
options: The broad white cloud looks like a camel with two humps.
A real camel is walking in the sky.
The cloud proves that camels can fly.
accepted_answers: The broad white cloud looks like a camel with two humps.
the white cloud looks like a camel

bridge.teaching_block: Use one movement detail and one comparison. The comparison should fit the shape described.
bridge.passage: Seen: thin cloud moving over water. Imagined: a silver boat.
options: A thin cloud glides over the water like a silver boat.
A silver boat turns into weather.
The cloud is under a boat in the lake.
accepted_answers: A thin cloud glides over the water like a silver boat.
the thin cloud looks like a silver boat

masterclass.teaching_block: Select writing that separates fact from imagination and explains the picture with a matching detail.
masterclass.passage: Seen: three small clouds in a row. Imagined: ducklings.
masterclass.prompt: Which description is accurate and vivid?
options: Three small clouds in a row look like ducklings following one another.
Three ducklings certainly live inside the clouds.
The sky has one enormous elephant.
accepted_answers: Three small clouds in a row look like ducklings following one another.
the row of small clouds looks like ducklings

independent_check.teaching_block: Write from a new observation. Include the seen colour or shape and a fitting comparison. Different clear wording can succeed.
independent_check.passage: Observation card: orange cloud at sunset; long curved shape; imagined canoe.
independent_check.prompt: Describe the wavy reflection in one vivid sentence.

concept_slots.description: Includes the orange colour or sunset setting.
Includes the long curved shape.
Compares the cloud to a canoe.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer observation-plus-imagination writing to a puddle reflection. State what is seen and what it resembles.
transfer_check.passage: Reflection card: yellow streetlight; wavy line in water; imagined golden snake.

concept_slots.description: Includes the yellow streetlight or its reflection.
Includes the wavy line in water.
Compares it to a golden snake.

items.passage: A white cloud grows wider as it moves above the school roof.
Three dark clouds move north. A small bright cloud stays near the sun.
A thin cloud splits into two pieces before both pieces fade.
items.prompt: What happens before the pieces fade?

items.passage: At noon the cloud is above the tower; later it moves beyond the hills.
A cloud has a round middle and eight thin arms spreading out.
Two tall cloud shapes stand side by side with a low curve between them.
A cloud has a broad top and one narrow stem below it.
items.prompt: What might it look like? Give the object and the clue.

concept_slots.description: Identifies an umbrella, mushroom, or tree as a sensible shape.
Uses the broad top and narrow stem.

items.passage: A shadow has a long body and a triangle at one end like a tail.
items.prompt: What might the shadow resemble, and why?

concept_slots.description: Identifies a kite, fish, or arrow as a sensible shape.
Uses the long body and triangle tail.

items.passage: Clouds scatter until they are spread far apart.
A brilliant white edge shines strongly in the sunlight.
The cloud expands, covering more and more of the sky.
A faint cloud is hard to see against the morning light.
The bright cloud floats above the hill.
items.prompt: Select the describing word in this sky sentence.

items.passage: Words: cloud / a / round / moon / like / looks
options: A round cloud looks like a moon.
Like a cloud round looks moon.
A moon cloud like round looks.
accepted_answers: A round cloud looks like a moon.
a round cloud looks like a moon

items.passage: Words: across / dark / hurry / clouds / the sky
items.prompt: Build the sentence about the dark clouds.
accepted_answers: dark clouds hurry across the sky
dark clouds hurry across the sky.

items.passage: Words: the / like / cloud / a fan / opens
items.prompt: Build the comparison about the fan-shaped cloud.
accepted_answers: the cloud opens like a fan
the cloud opens like a fan.

items.passage: Seen: one tall cloud with a rounded top. Imagined: an ice-cream cone.
items.prompt: Which sentence is careful and vivid?
options: The tall cloud looks like an ice-cream cone.
Ice cream is falling from the sky.
The cloud is truly frozen food.
accepted_answers: The tall cloud looks like an ice-cream cone.
the cloud looks like an ice cream cone

items.passage: Seen: tiny clouds moving in a line. Imagined: ants.
options: Tiny clouds move in a line like marching ants.
One huge cloud looks like a mountain.
accepted_answers: Tiny clouds move in a line like marching ants.
the tiny clouds look like ants

items.passage: Observation: pink cloud; two wide sides; imagined butterfly.
items.prompt: Write one vivid sentence that keeps the observation and comparison clear.

concept_slots.description: Includes the pink colour.
Includes two wide sides or wings.
Compares the cloud to a butterfly.

items.passage: Observation: dark cloud; jagged lower edge; imagined mountain range.
items.prompt: Describe the jagged cloud with one vivid comparison.

concept_slots.description: Includes the dark colour.
Includes the jagged lower edge.
Compares the cloud to mountains.
